draft.title: Annuities as geometric series
card: An annuity is a series of equal payments made at regular intervals, such as $1000 deposited at the end of each year. Interest is added each period at a rate r.
The future value is the total of all payments after compounding. A payment made with k periods left grows to M(1 + r)^k, so each payment is compounded for a different number of periods.
Written from the last payment back, the terms are M, M(1 + r), M(1 + r)², and so on. This is a geometric series with first term M and common ratio (1 + r). Its sum is FV = M[(1 + r)ⁿ − 1] ÷ r.
draft.remember: Each payment compounds for a different time, and the total is a geometric series with ratio 1 + r.

a.q: $500 is paid at the end of each year for 3 years, with interest of 10% a year. What is the future value just after the last payment?
a.why: The payments grow to 500, 500 × 1.1 = 550 and 500 × 1.1² = 605. The total is 500 + 550 + 605 = $1655. $1500 ignores interest, and $1815 wrongly compounds the last payment as well.
a.clue: The last payment earns no interest, and the earlier ones earn more.

b.q: Priya deposits $200 at the end of each year for 4 years at 5% a year. Which expression gives the future value just after her last deposit?
b.why: The deposits form a geometric series with first term 200, ratio 1.05 and 4 terms. The sum is 200 × (1.05⁴ − 1) ÷ 0.05, which is about $862.03. 200 × 1.05⁴ compounds only one deposit, not all four.
b.clue: Use the geometric sum with 4 terms, and divide by r, not 1 + r.

problems.detail: The why says $1815 comes from also compounding the last payment. Compounding every payment one extra period gives 550 + 605 + 665.50 = $1820.50, not $1815, so the explanation of this distractor is wrong. Either change the distractor to $1820.50 or fix the why.
The clue ('4 terms' and 'divide by r, not 1 + r') rules out every distractor in turn, so it hands students the answer instead of hinting at it.
